about: Hand-curated mutual-defence commitments, from the treaty owners' own pages. A treaty obligation is not an automatic response: each party decides what action it takes. Review before relying on the member lists.

nato.label: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty, Article 5)
nato.clause: an armed attack against one or more members is considered an attack against all of them

csto.label: CSTO (Collective Security Treaty, Article 4)
csto.clause: an act of aggression against one member is considered an act of aggression against all members

us_japan.label: US-Japan Security Treaty
us_japan.clause: each party would act to meet the common danger if either is attacked in territories under Japanese administration
us_japan.source: US Department of State, US collective defense arrangements

us_korea.label: US-Republic of Korea Mutual Defense Treaty
us_korea.clause: each party would act to meet the common danger in the event of an armed attack on either
us_korea.source: US Department of State, US collective defense arrangements

us_philippines.label: US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty
us_philippines.clause: each party would act to meet the common danger in the event of an armed attack on either in the Pacific area
us_philippines.source: US Department of State, US collective defense arrangements

anzus.label: ANZUS Treaty
anzus.clause: each party would act to meet the common danger in the event of an armed attack on any of them in the Pacific
anzus.source: US Department of State, US collective defense arrangements
anzus.note: New Zealand's obligations to the United States have been suspended since 1986.
